about.title: 21 years building ERP for construction
about.subtitle: Prizma is a powerful BPM, ERP, reporting and accounting platform — purpose-built for the construction industry and refined over two decades of real projects.
about.yearsBody: From the first procurement request to the final settlement, Prizma is shaped by how construction teams actually work.
about.storyBody1: Prizma began on construction sites, not in a boardroom. After 21 years working alongside contractors, we built a single platform that connects budgets, procurement, warehouses, finance and HR.
about.storyBody2: Today more than 5,000 users run their daily operations on Prizma — planning projects, routing approvals and tracking spend across every site in real time.

post1.author: Marina Volkova
post1.title: Cutting procurement cycle time by 40% on active sites
post1.excerpt: How transparent approval routes and historical price analysis help teams buy faster without overspending.
post1.lead: On a busy site, a slow purchase request is more than an annoyance — it stalls work, idles crews and quietly inflates cost. Here is how construction teams cut their procurement cycle by nearly half without adding headcount.
post1.quote: We stopped chasing approvals over the phone. The route does it for us, and everyone can see exactly where a request stands.

sections.heading: Where the time actually goes
sections.body: Most delays aren't in the buying itself — they're in the waiting. Requests sit in inboxes, approvers are unclear, and nobody knows who is holding things up. Mapping the real route from request to purchase order almost always reveals two or three steps that add days but no value.

sections.heading: Routes and price history do the heavy lifting
sections.body: With rule-based approval routes, each request goes to the right person automatically and escalates if it stalls. Pair that with historical price analysis, and buyers negotiate from real numbers instead of guesswork — faster decisions, better prices, and a full audit trail behind every order.

post2.author: Daniel Roth
post2.title: Actual cost vs. budget: catching overruns before they hurt
post2.excerpt: A field-tested framework for tracking spend against budget in real time across every project.
post2.lead: Budget overruns rarely arrive as a surprise — the signals are there for weeks before they show up in the final report. The trick is to see them while you can still act.
post2.quote: By the time an overrun reaches the monthly report, it's history. We needed to see it on the day it happened.

sections.heading: Compare in real time, not in hindsight
sections.body: A monthly reconciliation tells you what already went wrong. Comparing committed and actual cost against budget continuously turns budgeting into an early-warning system — deviations surface in days, not at month-end.

sections.heading: One number everyone trusts
sections.body: When procurement, finance and site managers all read the same live figure, arguments about whose spreadsheet is right disappear. Decisions get faster because the data is shared, current, and traceable down to the individual purchase order.

post3.author: Prizma Product Team
post3.title: What's new in Prizma: mobile approvals and live dashboards
post3.excerpt: A look at the latest release — approve requests on the go and watch project health update live.
post3.lead: This release is all about speed — getting decisions out of the office and giving managers a live view of every project, wherever they are.
post3.quote: Approvals that used to wait for someone to get back to their desk now happen from the cab of a truck.

sections.heading: Approve from anywhere
sections.body: Mobile approvals let managers review and sign off on procurement, payment and HR requests directly from their phone. Each request carries its full context — amounts, attachments and history — so decisions are informed, not rushed.

sections.heading: Dashboards that update themselves
sections.body: The new live dashboards refresh as data changes, showing budget health, open requests and project progress at a glance. No more exporting to a spreadsheet to find out where things stand.

post4.author: Aigerim Suleimenova
post4.title: Tracking field hours and payroll without the spreadsheets
post4.excerpt: Collect work hours from site, manage leave and run monthly payroll from a single source of truth.
post4.lead: Field hours scattered across paper timesheets and WhatsApp messages make payroll a monthly scramble. Bringing them into one place changes both accuracy and morale.
post4.quote: Payroll used to take a week of cross-checking. Now the hours are already in the system when we close the month.

sections.heading: Capture hours where the work happens
sections.body: Collecting work hours directly from site — with the right project and budget code attached — means payroll starts from clean data. No re-keying, no lost timesheets, no end-of-month reconstruction.

sections.heading: Leave, documents and payroll in one flow
sections.body: When leave requests, document tracking and payroll live in the same system, HR stops stitching tools together. Monthly payroll sheets generate from data that's already verified, and every figure traces back to its source.

post5.author: Daniel Roth
post5.title: Bringing banks, cash and contractors into one ledger
post5.excerpt: Why integrated finance beats disconnected tools when margins are tight and timelines are tighter.
post5.lead: Disconnected finance tools feel cheap until reconciliation season — then the hidden cost of moving numbers between systems becomes painfully clear.
post5.quote: Every handoff between two systems is a place for an error to hide. We removed the handoffs.

sections.heading: The real cost of disconnected tools
sections.body: When banking, cash, credits and contractor settlements live in separate places, every report is a manual merge. That's slow, error-prone, and impossible to audit quickly when a question comes up.

sections.heading: One ledger, end to end
sections.body: Integrating bank operations with contractor settlements and project costs means money is tracked from commitment to payment in a single ledger. Reconciliation becomes a review, not a reconstruction, and cash position is always current.

post6.author: Marina Volkova
post6.title: Five signs your construction firm has outgrown spreadsheets
post6.excerpt: If these problems sound familiar, it may be time to move your operations onto a real ERP.
post6.lead: Spreadsheets are where most construction businesses start — and there's nothing wrong with that, until the cracks start to cost you real money. Here are the signals worth watching for.
post6.quote: The spreadsheet didn't fail loudly. It just quietly stopped being the truth.

sections.heading: When data stops being trustworthy
sections.body: Multiple versions of the same file, broken formulas, and figures nobody can quite explain are the first signs. If teams second-guess the numbers before every meeting, the tool is no longer serving you.

sections.heading: When growth makes it worse
sections.body: Each new project, site and team member multiplies the manual work. An integrated ERP turns that scaling curve around — adding a project becomes a setting, not another spreadsheet to maintain by hand.
